summary: Chang Moi is the old trading and workshop district between Chiang Mai’s Old City moat and the Ping River. Its back lanes mix long-running businesses with craft workshops, cafés, galleries and street art. Treat this as an informal neighborhood wander, with no single attraction or dependable street-wide opening schedule.
whyGo: See everyday shophouse streets and working workshops alongside newer independent cafés and creative spaces.
The district makes an easy on-foot link between Tha Phae Gate, Warorot Market and the Ping River area.
bestFor: Travelers who enjoy unhurried neighborhood walks, small businesses and street photography.
A flexible morning outing that can finish with food and shopping at Warorot Market.
skipIf: You want a landmark with guaranteed exhibits, opening hours or a curated route.
You need a confirmed continuous step-free path or quiet pedestrian-only streets.
duration: Allow 1–2 hours on foot, including a coffee stop; this is a planning estimate. Add time if you continue browsing Warorot Market.
cost: Walking is free. Café, workshop and shopping costs vary by business; no district-wide ticket or reliable current price list applies.
hours: The lanes are public streets, but individual cafés, galleries and workshops set their own hours. The local guide recommends mornings, when more workshops are working; check a specific stop directly.
bestTime: Choose a weekday morning for cooler walking and a better chance of seeing workshops at work. The lanes are described as quieter than the main roads, which carry through traffic.
gettingThere: Start near Tha Phae Gate, then walk east through Chang Moi’s side lanes toward the river and finish at Warorot Market. A Chiang Mai resident’s September 2026 guide estimates Tha Phae Gate and Warorot each about 5 minutes from the district, the river about 10 minutes, and recommends an hour or two to wander; exact times depend on your route and pace. From elsewhere, take a red songthaew, taxi or ride-hail to Tha Phae Gate or Chang Moi, then continue on foot.
booking: No booking or admission is needed for the neighborhood walk. Confirm a café, gallery or workshop directly if you are planning around it; no current district-wide visitor service was identified.
accessibility: Formal accessibility information for the lanes was not found. Expect normal urban sidewalks, road crossings, possible uneven surfaces and active traffic on through-roads; shop entrances may have steps or narrow interiors. A continuous step-free route is not confirmed.
practicalTips: Use Tha Phae Gate as a simple starting point and head east through the lanes toward Warorot; the precise route is best chosen as you walk, since individual venues change.
Look for workshops and businesses with shutters open, but ask before photographing people, workspaces or interiors; keep entrances and sidewalks clear.
Carry water and some cash for small purchases. Treat the lanes as lived-in streets and yield to motorbikes and delivery traffic.
Pair the walk with Warorot Market, but check its schedule separately because the market has its own hours.
decemberNotes: December 2026 is a good season to plan an outdoor morning walk, but no special December 2026 hours or street event for Chang Moi’s lanes was confirmed. Businesses may set their own holiday hours and year-end traffic may affect rides; check any chosen stop shortly before visiting.
uncertainties: The neighborhood has no published street-wide opening hours or fixed walking itinerary; shop and workshop hours vary.
Walking times come from a resident’s neighborhood guide and are broad estimates, not turn-by-turn directions.
Accessibility conditions vary by street and business; no step-free route survey was found.
The photo is a 2014 Commons photograph of Chang Moi Kao Road, an authentic district streetscape, rather than a documented view of a specific back lane; buildings and businesses may have changed.
